summary: Bonner County, ID lookout: 1922 cabin, 1935 30-foot L-4 tower, destroyed 1964; footings reported on the summit, no tower left standing.

facts.design: 30-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, replacing a 1922 frame cabin
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1964; site photo captions mention footings on the summit

access.note: WillhiteWeb gives driving directions and a walk to the site and notes no closure; no source states the legal access status

visit.trail_note: Drive up State Highway 57 and Stone Johnny Road to an old parking spot, then walk the overgrown last half mile. No tower remains to climb.

events.note: 12-by-12-foot frame cabin; communication wires run to the site
Cupola roof put on the cabin in place of the gable roof, per Peterson; two other sources date the cupola to 1925
Henry A. Peterson posted as lookout for the 1925 season; Tom Terrell sent up as smokechaser to help with the roof
30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab replaces the cabin
Tower destroyed; four sources agree on the year
USGS benchmark placed at the highest point, using the old footings as reference marks

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts describe a cupola cabin from 1922. Peterson, who was there in 1925, describes a gable-roofed cabin whose roof was replaced with a cupola that summer, and the Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb pages also date the cupola to 1925. The story follows the 1925 date and reports the disagreement.

firelookout.com puts the lookout 4 miles north of Priest River; the 1922 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts says five miles, and WillhiteWeb's directions run 5 miles up Highway 57. The story gives four to five miles.

sources.title: Early Days in the Forest Service, Volume 4: Early-Day Ranger in the Priest Lake Country (Henry A. Peterson)

notes_for_editor: Destroyed in 1964; no tower stands. Cupola date disputed: Peterson (first-hand, 1925) and two later pages say 1925; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say a cupola cabin in 1922. Distance from Priest River is 4 miles on one source and 5 on two others. Legal access status is not stated in any source, so the level is 'unknown' even though WillhiteWeb's directions reach the site with no closure noted; verify with the Kaniksu National Forest before publishing. Footings claim rests on photo captions with no visit date. Not used: uidaho Priest River Historical Collection items priestriver0217 and priestriver0218 (possibly this lookout, unidentified).
